title: A GUI with a QC queue must expose a 'recently QC'd' view backed by the QC archive
requirement: If a Clank's GUI exposes a QC queue, it MUST also expose an operator-visible view of recently-made QC decisions (a dedicated route or an inline section on the same page is both acceptable), sourced from the QC decision archive, not reconstructed from the live operational table.
rationale: Present in 8 of 9 surveyed Clanks in some form (dedicated route, inline section, or API endpoint), and its absence is meaningfully correlated with the one Clank that also lacks a QC archive entirely (smartphone-clank) — reinforcing that this is a load-bearing part of the archival contract (STD-UI-COM-002), not decoration. It gives operators a way to audit/undo-check recent decisions without needing DB access, and lets the operator verify STD-UI-COM-003 is actually working.
forbidden: A QC queue GUI with no way to see recently-decided items short of querying the database directly
acceptance: A route, tab, or section exists that lists recent QC decisions
It reads from the QC archive/decision record, not by inferring 'recent' from the live table

evidence.summary: Dedicated QC History tab, excludes corrected rows by default.
Dedicated nav item and route, own template, reads only from the archive DB.
Inline section or dedicated route in every other surveyed Clank that has a QC queue at all.
No 'recently QC'd' view of any kind — consistent with having no QC archive to source it from (see STD-UI-COM-002 counter-evidence).

notes: Pass 1 candidate. Deliberately does not mandate a dedicated route vs. an inline section — that is presentation, not contract.
